meta.tagline: A glass skyline rising from the desert, beside a one-dirham ferry

pills: From gold souk to man-made islands

overview.title: Welcome to Dubai
overview.intro: Dubai tells two stories at once: one is the glass-and-steel future gazing down from Burj Khalifa's 828 meters; the other is the past of the wooden abra crossing the Creek for one dirham. Fifty years ago this was a pearl divers' town; today it is the world's fastest-built showcase — but don't let the showcase make you skip the old part: Deira's spice-scented souks, the wind-tower courtyards of Al Fahidi and a glass of karak tea show where the city's heart still beats. The way to love Dubai is to visit both banks.

local_word.definition: Arabic for 'my dear': the word you'll hear a hundred times a day in Dubai. The taxi driver, the waiter, the souk merchant call everyone habibi — it is the common currency of warmth, bargaining and friendship. When someone says 'yes habibi' to you, smile: the Gulf's door has just opened.

rules.title: Build the schedule around the air conditioning
rules.description: Dubai has two seasons: outdoors and indoors. November to March is an open-air paradise; in summer the street hits 45°C at noon — put outdoor plans before 10 a.m. and after sunset, and give the remaining hours to museums, malls and the aquarium.

rules.title: Don't skip Old Dubai
rules.description: The Burj and the marina are the city's showcase; the Creek is its soul: Al Fahidi's narrow lanes, the abra ride, the spice and gold souks fit into half a day — the city's most authentic half day. See new Dubai from the sky, old Dubai from water level.

rules.title: Respect the rules and the etiquette
rules.description: Dubai is a relaxed city, but it has its manners: dress modestly around mosques and government buildings, don't photograph people without permission, avoid rowdiness in public. If you come during Ramadan, eat and drink indoors by day — respect given is respect returned.

quick_facts.label: Airport
quick_facts.sub: The red metro line runs downtown

quick_facts.label: Currency
quick_facts.sub: Cards everywhere; the abra wants cash

tip.label: The Dubai philosophy
tip.text: This city has the 'biggest' of everything, but the best moments are small: a one-dirham abra crossing, a desert sunset, the steam over a karak glass. See the records — but collect your memories at the water's edge and in the dunes.

transport.title: Getting Around
transport.intro: The city is a long ribbon: the metro carries the spine, taxis fill the gaps, the abra crosses the Creek for one dirham — and walking only works in season.

items.title: Arriving from the airport
items.description: DXB sits inside the city: board the red metro line at the terminal and ride straight to Downtown and the Marina. Taxis and Careem/Uber are fixed-rate and painless — the practical choice for late-night landings.

items.title: Metro and tram
items.description: The driverless metro runs the city ribbon end to end: get a Nol card; the Gold car buys comfort and there's a separate women-and-children car. On the Marina side, the tram and the Palm monorail take over — and the stations are air-conditioned.

items.title: Crossing the Creek by abra
items.description: Wooden abras have shuttled between Deira and Bur Dubai for a century: the crossing costs one dirham and is the city's best 'tour'. Cross from spice souk to gold souk over the water — Dubai's oldest transit line is still its most delightful.

items.title: Careem, Uber and taxis
items.description: App rides and the cream-colored official taxis are plentiful and reliable: everyone uses them even for short hops. They are the answer to every distance that looks unwalkable — in summer, even two blocks can be taxi territory.

items.title: Getting to the desert
items.description: Desert safaris, dunes and camp evenings lie 45 minutes from town: go with a licensed operator and choose a small group. Driving into the dunes yourself takes experience — leave the first time to a professional.

callout.label: Abra tip
callout.text: Board the abra at the Bur Dubai station in the late afternoon and cross toward Deira: dhows, minarets and glass towers gather in one frame in the sunset light. This one-dirham ride is the city's highest view-per-dirham ratio.

stay.title: Where to Stay
stay.intro: Dubai is a ribbon city; the choice runs between poles: Downtown's tower views, the Marina's beach rhythm, or the souk soul of the old town.

local_word.definition: The wind tower: the Gulf's natural cooling system before air conditioning. The towers caught the breeze and funneled it into the house — the barjeels crowning Al Fahidi's rooftops are monuments to Dubai's desert wisdom. You'll spot the form quoted in some new skyscrapers: the city cites its own past.

items.name: Downtown and around the Burj
items.description: Burj Khalifa, the giant mall and the fountain show at your doorstep: the city's most iconic views from your balcony. Linked everywhere by metro — the classic choice for a first visit.

items.name: Dubai Marina and JBR
items.description: A marina promenade between skyscrapers, beach and seaside cafes at JBR: the zone for a city holiday with swimming included. The evening promenade is one of the city's liveliest stages.

items.name: Old Dubai (Deira and Bur Dubai)
items.description: Both banks of the Creek: souks, abra stations and the city's most honestly priced hotels. No luxury, plenty of character — for seeing Dubai beyond the showcase.

items.name: Jumeirah coast
items.description: The low-rise shore strip: public beaches, the kite beach and the Burj Al Arab silhouette. Linked to the center by car — for a beach-first, calmer stay.

items.name: Business Bay
items.description: Canal-side hotels just south of Downtown: the Burj within walking distance, prices one notch kinder. The modern base for those weighing location against cost.

best_time.title: When to Go
best_time.intro: Dubai's calendar is a negotiation with the sun: November–March is open-air season; summer belongs to the air-conditioned indoor world and falling prices.

items.label: Spring
items.name: The Season's Graceful Finale
items.subtitle: Spring · Warm sea, heating desert
items.description: March is still a golden month: the sea has warmed and the evenings are mild. Heat climbs through April and May, but morning and evening programs run comfortably. If Ramadan falls here, the iftar tents lend the city another kind of grace.

callout.label: Ramadan note
callout.text: If your visit meets Ramadan, join an iftar table: hotel and neighborhood iftar tents welcome guests, and the atmosphere is the warmest face of the year. Eat and drink indoors during daylight — respect is repaid with generosity.

items.label: Summer
items.name: Indoor Season
items.subtitle: Summer · 45°C outside, 22°C inside
items.description: Summer Dubai lives indoors: the mega-malls, aquarium, ski slope and museums are air-conditioned cities of their own. Hotels hit their yearly lows — for pool-over-beach, night-over-noon travelers, summer Dubai is surprisingly pleasant.

callout.label: Midday note
callout.text: Stubborn midday walking in summer is dangerous: dehydration is fast and distances deceive. Take a taxi even for two blocks and move outdoor plans past sunset — the night beaches are summer's hidden reward.

items.label: Autumn
items.name: The Doors Open
items.subtitle: Autumn · Softening air, opening terraces
items.description: In October the city moves outdoors: terraces are set, the beaches begin to fill, the desert camps open their season. November is the most balanced month for open-air plans — the heat has broken and high-season crowds haven't peaked.

callout.label: November tip
callout.text: Book your desert safari for the sunset session in November: the dunes turn gold and the camp evening runs cool. In town, a sunset walk on Kite Beach is the season's opening ritual — with the Burj Al Arab silhouette in attendance.

items.label: Winter
items.name: The Golden Season
items.subtitle: Winter · 25°C sunshine, the world convenes
items.description: December to February is when Dubai's promise comes true: 25°C sun by day, jacket-cool evenings. The Shopping Festival, New Year's fireworks and full beaches — the world is here, and the prices know it.

callout.label: January tip
callout.text: To watch the Burj Khalifa New Year's fireworks from Downtown, claim your spot hours early; for a calmer celebration, the Creek shore or a desert camp is the alternative. The Shopping Festival discounts run through January.

eat.title: What to Eat
eat.intro: The Dubai table is a port city's inheritance: the date-sweet generosity of Emirati cooking, the spices of the Indian quarter, and every cuisine on earth in one city.

local_word.definition: Strong tea boiled with milk and cardamom: the Gulf's daily ritual. It comes in a glass for a dirham or two, and the cafeterias' drive-up service is famous — the 'karak break' is Dubai's social institution. Don't leave without trying it: the city's warmest flavor is its cheapest.

items.name: Karak and chapati breakfast
items.description: Karak in a glass at an Old Dubai cafeteria, hot chapati and fried eggs alongside: a kingdom for a few dirhams. Join the morning workers' queue — this is the city's true breakfast salon.

items.name: Machboos and the Emirati table
items.description: Lamb or fish machboos over spiced rice, with dates and coffee as welcome: the generous classic of Emirati cooking. Try it at a traditional Emirati restaurant — the floor-cushion seating section is part of the experience.

items.name: Shawarma night
items.description: The Levantine masters' shawarma is the foundation of Dubai street food: garlicky toum, pickles and thin flatbread. A late-night queue outside a cafeteria is the best address marker in town.

items.name: Luqaimat
items.description: Fried sweet dough balls under date syrup and sesame: the calling card of Emirati dessert. Crisp outside, soft inside — the star of Ramadan, but good places serve it year-round.

items.name: The Friday brunch institution
items.description: The long brunch that opens the weekend is Dubai's social tradition: dozens of stations, a table that lasts hours. Options span every budget — booking is essential and appetite should be deployed strategically.

items.name: Thali at Meena Bazaar
items.description: Tray thalis, dosas and fresh tandoor bread in Bur Dubai's Indian quarter: the city's oldest migrant kitchen at its most honest prices. Join the local office crowd at noon — the tray comes full and the bill light.

callout.label: Table rule
callout.text: In Dubai the same dish has three prices: expensive on a mall floor, very expensive on the beachfront, honest at a neighborhood cafeteria. Save the Michelin night as its own plan; for everyday flavor, the cafeteria and the ethnic quarters always win.

hidden_gems.title: Hidden Corners
hidden_gems.intro: Everyone sees the Burj; these six are Dubai's waterside, desert-scented hidden face.

items.name: The abra crossing
items.description: You sit shoulder to shoulder on the wooden boat and glide to the far bank to the putter of the motor: spice scents, dhow silhouettes and minarets keep you company. Dubai's oldest line remains its cheapest and most authentic experience.

items.name: Al Fahidi Historical Neighbourhood
items.description: Houses of coral stone and gypsum, barjeel towers, shaded courtyards: old Dubai's restored quarter. Wander between the coffee museum and the small galleries — in the morning hours you'll have it nearly to yourself.

items.name: Alserkal Avenue
items.description: Galleries, an independent cinema and third-wave coffee in the Al Quoz warehouse district: the heart of Dubai's contemporary art scene. Saturday afternoons are its liveliest — the city's creativity beyond the showcase lives here.

items.name: Ras Al Khor Wildlife Sanctuary
items.description: Hundreds of flamingos at the foot of the skyscraper skyline: you watch the pink flock from free observation hides. Winter is peak guest season — Dubai's most unexpected postcard.

items.name: The Deira souks at morning
items.description: The sack scents of the spice souk, the window blaze of the gold souk, and the dhow wharf's porters at the edge: old trading Dubai is most itself in the morning hours. Bargaining is the custom — accept the offered tea.

items.name: Kite Beach and the public beaches
items.description: Swim at the free public beach, walk the running track, watch the Burj Al Arab silhouette at sunset: Dubai beach life without a ticket. Grab something from the food trucks — the beach evening assembles itself.

callout.label: Two-bank strategy
callout.text: The formula for a balanced Dubai: one day of showcase (Burj, mall, Marina), one day of soul (Creek, souks, Al Fahidi, cafeteria). Don't compress both into one day — the city tells its story at two different tempos.

traps.title: Tourist Traps
traps.intro: Dubai is safe and orderly; its traps are not dangerous but expensive — know these four and protect your budget.

items.name: Buying the Burj ticket at the door
items.description: A last-minute At the Top ticket at the counter means both a queue and peak pricing; sunset slots sell out weeks ahead.
items.instead: Buy a timed ticket online days ahead; if sunset is gone, the first morning slots are calm and clear. Alternative: a cafe terrace facing the tower delivers the view at a fraction of the price.

items.name: The cheapest desert safari
items.description: Cut-price safaris deliver a crowded convoy, rushed dune driving and a conveyor-belt camp evening; the experience bears no relation to the brochure photo.
items.instead: Choose a licensed operator running small groups in the protected reserve; ask in advance about the sunset session and the camp menu. Slightly more money buys an entirely different desert.

items.name: The 'copy bag' invitation in the souk
items.description: In Deira and the tourist zones the 'copy bag, copy watch' whisper invites you into back rooms: quality uncertain, bargaining loaded, the situation legally gray.
items.instead: Smile and keep walking. Do your souk shopping in spices, dates, gold and fabric — their bargaining is legitimate and their quality in plain view. On gold, check the hallmark stamp.

items.name: Estimating distances off the map
items.description: Between two points that look close on the map may lie a shadeless highway, an interchange and a construction site; a 'ten-minute walk' becomes an ordeal in summer.
items.instead: Save walking for the neighborhoods (the Marina promenade, the Creek shore, Al Fahidi); connect the dots by metro and taxi. In summer, add at least fifty percent to any walking estimate.

callout.label: Golden rule
callout.text: Money evaporates fast in Dubai, but it doesn't have to: most of the best experiences — the abra, the public beach, the souk, karak — cost a few dirhams. Save luxury for one or two chosen moments and live the rest in the city's cheap, authentic layer.

itinerary.title: Ready-Made Itineraries
itinerary.intro: If you hate planning, follow these flows. Times are flexible; keep the spirit, break the order.

plans.title: If You Have 1 Day
plans.subtitle: From the Creek's soul to the Burj's summit

steps.title: Karak and chapati morning
steps.description: Karak in a glass and hot chapati at a Bur Dubai cafeteria: start the day with the city's warmest flavor.

steps.title: Al Fahidi and the abra crossing
steps.description: A morning walk in the wind-tower quarter, then the one-dirham abra to the Deira bank: bargaining practice in the spice and gold souks.

steps.title: Meena Bazaar lunch
steps.description: Thali or dosa in the Indian quarter: the tray full, the bill light. Wait out the midday heat indoors.

steps.title: Dubai Mall and the aquarium
steps.description: The aquarium tunnel and the waterfall in the air-conditioned mega-world: a cool interlude until Burj time.

steps.title: The top of Burj Khalifa
steps.description: At the Top with your timed ticket: see the city between desert and sea from above at sunset.

steps.title: Fountain show and a shawarma finale
steps.description: Watch the musical fountains on Burj Lake; close with a toum-laced shawarma at a neighborhood cafeteria — showcase and soul in a single day.

plans.title: If You Have 3 Days
plans.subtitle: Showcase, desert and sea — the full Dubai

steps.title: Classic Dubai
steps.description: The 1-day flow above: karak morning, Al Fahidi, the abra and the souks, Burj Khalifa, the fountain show.

steps.title: Sea and marina day
steps.description: Morning swim and beach walk at Kite Beach; a fish lunch on the Jumeirah side; the Marina promenade and the Palm monorail with Atlantis views in the afternoon; seaside dinner at JBR.

steps.title: Desert and farewell
steps.description: Morning at the Alserkal Avenue galleries + the Ras Al Khor flamingos; afternoon small-group desert safari — sunset on the dunes, an Emirati spread and stars at camp; dates and spices in the suitcase on the way home — the city lights look different from the desert.

phrases.title: 5-Word Survival Kit
phrases.intro: Dubai's daily language is English, but Arabic greetings win hearts; these five are the keys to Gulf etiquette.

items.meaning: Hello — the door-opening greeting of Gulf Arabic
Thank you — valid from cafeteria to souk
My dear, my friend — the common currency of warmth; smile when you hear it
Done, finished, deal — the closing word of every bargain
God willing — plan, hope and courtesy in one; the Gulf's timekeeper
